input.quote: Such books and records shall be kept for at least three (3) years following the end of the calendar month to which they pertain, and shall be open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio for the purpose of verifying the amounts payable to Commerce One under this Agreement. Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit/inspection right binding us (Corio, as licensee/payor), and it already tracks the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at no more than once each calendar year; the audit is conducted by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to us; it must occur at reasonable times; Commerce One bears all costs and expenses unless an underpayment of more than five percent (5%) is revealed (better than the 10% fallback trigger); and the right extends only to books of accounts and records for verifying amounts payable — there is no right of direct or remote access to our systems, so no walk-away issue. The only sub-element short of preferred is that notice is expressed as "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30 (or 15) days; notice is nonetheless required, so audits cannot be unannounced. We note this as a drafting nicety rather than a deviation and do not propose a redline.
